results.reason: Cites §2.2 auto-renewal for five years with the 270/240-day window. Calculates it as about Oct 3 to Nov 2, 2026 against the June 30, 2027 expiry. Explains a lock-in for five more years with the purchase minimum. Recommends a signed extension or a protective non-renewal notice.

Cites §5.3's 30-day objection right and deemed acceptance. Gives Aug 21 receipt, so the deadline was Sept 20, 2026. Says the window appears lapsed, says to confirm with the client whether an objection was sent, and recommends a commercial negotiation.

Explains that §11.1 has no fault limiter and could cover Brightmere design-defect claims. Notes it is uncapped via §12.3(a) while Brightmere's §11.2 indemnity is capped. Recommends narrowing to Halvorsen's fault and making the cap treatment reciprocal.

Identifies Amendment §3.1 replacing §12.3 and deleting the §9.3 recall carve-out. Notes recall reimbursement is now subject to the 12-month cap, which a large recall could exceed. Recommends restoring §12.3(b).
Identifies Amendment §6's Delaware law and Wilmington forum, in conflict with Agr. §17's New York law and forum. Notes §1.4 means Delaware likely prevails. Recommends restoring New York.
States the Notice was delivered by FedEx on Aug 21, 2026.
States the Initial Term ends June 30, 2027.
States that Agr. §1.4 ranks amendments first.
Memo addressed to the Partner. Issues consistently give a Where (document and section), a why-it-matters, and a recommended fix.
Concludes the recall reimbursement is now capped.
Acknowledges the Delaware provisions and concludes Delaware likely prevails.
